title: Inside Celiac
author: Celiac Disease Foundation
description:
Celiac disease has never had a platform — or a voice — quite like this.
Inside Celiac is a new signature series from the Celiac Disease Foundation hosted by acclaimed actress Katie Lowes, known to millions for her standout roles in Scandal, Inventing Anna, and The Hunting Wives. Katie will bring her star power, extraordinary ability to connect with audiences, and deeply personal experience living with celiac disease to candid conversations that put this often-overlooked condition in the national spotlight.
Through this compelling themed series, Katie will sit down with leading medical and nutrition experts, patients, advocates, and other influential voices to explore what it truly means to live with celiac disease, from the long road to diagnosis and the everyday realities of the gluten-free diet to emotional health, family life, groundbreaking research, and the urgent search for treatments beyond the diet.
By pairing Katie’s recognizable voice and powerful storytelling with the Celiac Disease Foundation’s trusted expertise and international reach, Inside Celiac will inform, inspire, and engage audiences across the globe — giving millions of people greater visibility, a stronger voice, and a place to feel seen and heard.

description:
The Posture Reset: Small Habits for a Healthier Day is a wellness podcast dedicated to helping people build better posture habits, improve body awareness, and create more comfortable daily routines. Designed for office professionals, remote workers, students, gamers, and anyone who spends long hours sitting or looking at screens, this series explores practical ways to make posture awareness part of everyday life.Each episode covers topics such as desk ergonomics, healthy sitting habits, screen positioning, gentle stretching, movement breaks, neck and shoulder comfort, and the importance of consistency when developing healthier routines.

Listeners will learn how small adjustments to their workspace and daily schedule can encourage better movement habits without requiring a complete lifestyle overhaul.To make these habits easier to maintain, the podcast also highlights digital tools such as the Posturly Posture Reminder App, which offers smart posture reminders, posture analysis, progress tracking, and guided exercises to support a more consistent approach to posture awareness. By combining practical wellness education with simple technology-assisted routines, the series encourages listeners to check in with their bodies throughout the day.

Whether you are working at a computer, studying for exams, or enjoying extended gaming sessions, The Posture Reset offers realistic ideas for making movement, alignment, and self-awareness a regular part of your routine. The goal is to promote sustainable habits, encourage active breaks, and help listeners approach everyday posture with greater confidence and consistency.

title: Solve For...
author: Nova Institute for Health
description:
What would it mean to create a world where health is valued as our most essential asset? A future where people, places, and our planet can truly flourish? Sometimes, all it takes is a tiny change, a local fix, or a spark of innovation to help us think differently. Solve For... is all about finding those emerging possibilities and embracing the power of curiosity to bring health and well-being into focus in unexpected new ways. 
Join acclaimed journalist Kate Morgan and Nova Institute for Health president Brian Berman, MD, as they highlight the innovators tackling solutions to our most complex challenges at the intersection of medicine, biology, neuroscience, nutrition, the arts, and more. 
In an era of overwhelm, change doesn't have to be huge to be meaningful. It just has to start somewhere.
Hosts: 
Kate Morgan is a freelance journalist based in Pennsylvania. Her reporting has appeared in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, National Geographic, BBC, Popular Science, Sierra, and many other publications. Kate's work takes a broad view of health and often focuses on the inherent optimism of those working to repair and restore natural ecosystems and human communities.
Brian Berman, MD, is the president of the Nova Institute for Health, which he founded in 2007 to catalyze new ideas in health. He is professor emeritus at the University of Maryland School of Medicine, where he was the director of the Center for Integrative Medicine. Dr. Berman has served as an advisor to the NIH, chairing and subsequently serving for three terms on the advisory committee to the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health. He cofounded and, for 25 years, directed the complementary medicine field of Cochrane, an internationally recognized leader in evidence-based medicine. Dr. Berman is also the recipient of the prestigious Bravewell Leadership Award, which celebrates and supports visionaries who have committed their medical careers to transforming health care in America.
Solve For...is a production of the Nova Institute for Health. Written and produced by Kate Morgan. Editing and sound design by Olanre Adewole. Executive producers: Brian Berman and Sue Berman. To learn more, visit novainstituteforhealth.org.

title: Wellness Without Wine
author: Deirdre
description:
Wellness Without Wine with Deirdre Coyne

What if life could feel better without wine at the centre of it?

Welcome to Wellness Without Wine, a podcast for women who want to rethink their relationship with alcohol and discover a healthier, happier and more fulfilling way to live.

I'm Deirdre Coyne, a Sober Coach and Positive Psychology Coach. Drawing on psychology, mindset and behaviour change, I'll explore why we reach for wine, how everyday habits become part of our lives, and how we can begin to make different choices.

Together, we'll look at the role alcohol can play in stress, switching off, confidence, emotional wellbeing and our sense of identity. We'll explore practical strategies to help you understand your habits, reconnect with what matters to you and create more of the things you want in life.

Expect honest conversations, bite-sized podshots, practical reflections and deeper dives into the psychology of change.

This isn't about judgement or perfection. It's about curiosity, self-understanding and discovering what life could look like when you start putting your own wellbeing first.

Because this isn't just about drinking less or living without wine. It's about creating a life you genuinely enjoy.

Wellness Without Wine — a fresh perspective on alcohol, mindset and your next chapter.

title: Remembrance Record

description: The Remembrance Record is where legacy becomes inheritance. Andrea B. Denney — legacy preservation artist, national award-winning fine art photographer, and 17-year caregiver through her husband's home hospice — walks with widows and widowers who refuse to let the second loss happen: the one where the phone dies, the cloud overwrites, and you press play to silence. Voice preservation, legacy archives, and the Move With philosophy. Because you don't move on from the people you love. You move with them.

title: The Jack Benny Program
author: Golden Replay
description:
Step into the world of The Jack Benny Program, where a perfectly timed pause can be as funny as a punch line. Jack Benny stars as a famously penny-pinching, eternally 39-year-old entertainer whose oversized confidence in his violin playing is matched only by his reluctance to spend a dime.
Joining Jack are the quick-witted Rochester, played by Eddie Anderson, along with Mary Livingstone, announcer Don Wilson, bandleader Phil Harris, and singer Dennis Day. Together, they turn everyday misunderstandings, show-business rivalries, and Jack’s bruised ego into classic comedy.
With memorable running jokes, playful banter, and an unforgettable cast, The Jack Benny Program remains one of old-time radio’s most beloved comedies.

title: Beyond the Spectrum.. every age, every need

description:
Beyond the Spectrum is the evolution of Just Two Dads, a podcast born from heartfelt conversations between fathers navigating life, family, and community. What began as a dialogue about parenting and stewardship has grown into a broader mission: to explore the full spectrum of human experience, inclusion, and gratitude.


This new chapter bridges the familiar warmth and authenticity of Just Two Dads with a wider lens — amplifying voices, stories, and frameworks that multiply blessings for families, businesses, and communities. Each episode blends practical stewardship tools with mission-driven storytelling, offering listeners both inspiration and actionable steps to live with clarity, discipline, and connection.


Whether you’ve been with us since the beginning or are joining for the first time, Beyond the Spectrum invites you to step into a space where gratitude meets action, and where every story becomes a resource for building trust, resilience, and community. title: Between The Forks
author: CLARK Material Handling Company
description:
Welcome to Between The Forks, the official podcast from CLARK — the original inventor of the forklift and a global leader in material handling innovation.  For more than a century, CLARK has built the machines and the momentum that keep industries moving. Now, we’re taking you beyond the warehouse floor to explore the ideas, technologies, and people shaping the next century of lift trucks and logistics. 


Each episode, we:


• Break down the latest in drivetrain, battery, safety, and automation technologies
• Talk with industry experts, operators, and leaders who keep supply chains running
• Unpack real-world applications, operational insights, and lessons learned from the field
• Explore how efficiency, safety, and sustainability are redefining the way the world moves 


From legacy engineering to next-generation innovation, Between The Forks brings you an inside look at the evolution of an industry CLARK helped create — and continues to lead.  Whether you manage a fleet, move materials, or simply want to understand the machinery that powers the global economy, this is your inside track to the world that moves the world.

Through engaging conversations with scientists, healthcare professionals, innovators, and changemakers, we uncover the science, stories, and perspectives that help us better understand what shapes our well-being. Together, we explore everything from environmental toxins and chronic disease to nutrition, women’s health, emerging science, and the power of community and connection. description:
”Let’s Talk ” is a ground breaking podcast that dives deep into the often-unspoken realms of mental health and wellbeing. Hosted by Vaishalli Paatil, a former dentist turned filmmaker and storyteller, this show brings to light the shadows that hold us back and the strength that propels us forward.
Each episode features raw, honest conversations of my own journey along with guests from all walks of life, sharing mental health journeys, challenges, and triumphs. Vaishalli’s unique background in healthcare and creative storytelling allows her to approach these sensitive topics with both empathy and insight.
From exploring the impact of cultural expectations on mental well-being to discussing practical mindfulness techniques, ”Let’s Talk” covers a wide range of topics relevant to anyone seeking to improve their mental wellbeing. The show also provides valuable resources and expert advice, empowering listeners to take control of their mental well-being.
Whether you’re struggling with your own mental health, supporting a loved one, or simply interested in personal growth, ”Let’s Talk” offers a wealth of, information, inspiration, and tools to help you navigate life’s challenges and discover your inner strength.
Join us as we break stigmas, share stories, and listen to the voices that need to be heard. It’s time to talk and we are here to listen.

title: MyStreaksMoney

description:
MyStreaksMoney is the podcast about building financial strength through the power of consistency.
Managing money doesn't have to be complicated, overwhelming, or restrictive. You don't need to completely overhaul your financial life overnight. You need a few simple things you can do consistently.
Hosted by Jeffery J. Downs, co-author of Streaking, the MyStreaksMoney Podcast applies the principles of Streaking to your money—helping you create simple financial behaviors, keep a record of what matters, and build momentum one small action at a time.
From budgeting and spending to saving, debt, investing, and preparing for the future, each episode explores practical ways to strengthen your relationship with money without relying on willpower, motivation, or perfection.
Because financial freedom isn't built in one big moment.
It's built one streak at a time

author: Mark Howard

Great leadership doesn’t happen by accident. Great customer service doesn’t happen by accident. Great cultures don’t happen by accident.

Welcome to Never By Accident, a podcast hosted by Mark Howard about becoming more intentional in how we lead, serve, develop people, and live. Drawing from more than 25 years of leadership and management experience, Mark shares practical lessons, real-world stories, successes, failures, and conversations about what it takes to build teams and organizations where people truly matter.

Each episode explores topics such as leadership, workplace culture, customer experience, employee development, consistency, accountability, personal growth, and the everyday decisions that shape the kind of leader—and person—you become. Whether you're leading an organization, managing a team, running a shift, building a business, or simply trying to become better at what you do, Never By Accident is built around one simple belief: The things that matter most shouldn't be left to accident.

author: Jes | The Haunted Line
description:
Where history, hauntings, and folklore meet.

The Haunted Line explores the darker side of history... one haunted place, unsettling legend, and unexplained story at a time.

From abandoned hospitals and infamous murder houses to centuries-old cemeteries, historic inns, witch trials, folklore, and places where the past doesn't seem quite ready to stay buried, we dig into the real history behind the hauntings. Along the way, we'll separate documented fact from legend, explore the paranormal stories that have endured for generations, and share experiences from our own investigations of some of these places.

Because sometimes the truth is just as haunting as the ghost story.

Step across The Haunted Line.

title: Perfectly Imperfect
author: Marleny
description:
Perfectly Imperfect is a reminder that you don’t have to have your whole life figured out to be doing just fine. 🤍

In a world where everyone seems to have it all together, it’s easy to feel like you’re falling behind. We get so caught up in chasing the next big thing, comparing ourselves to others, and worrying about where we should be that we forget to appreciate where we are right now.

This podcast is about embracing the messy, beautiful, confusing reality of being human. The lessons, the setbacks, the little wins, the hard days, and everything in between. Because the truth is, we’re all just figuring it out as we go, and even when it doesn’t feel like it, we’re doing better than we think.

So take a breath, give yourself some grace, and remember that you don’t need to be perfect to be proud of yourself. You’re allowed to grow at your own pace, change your mind, make mistakes, and still appreciate the life you’re living.

You’re not behind. You’re not failing. You’re human. And that’s perfectly imperfect. ✨

title: WorkBuzz | The Employee Engagement Podcast
author: WorkBuzz
description:
Most engagement surveys tell you what your people think. WorkBuzz goes further, into what you do about it.

WorkBuzz is the employee engagement and People Science partner for HR leaders who won't settle for "we measured it." We work with organisations across the UK to help them understand what's really happening with their people and, more importantly, what to do next.

In this podcast, we cut through the noise around employee listening and get into what actually works: what the data shows, what high-maturity organisations do differently, and how HR and People teams can turn survey results into real action from managers and leaders.

Expect honest conversation, evidence-backed insight, and a clear focus on momentum not just measurement.

Who it's for: HR Directors, People leaders, and anyone making the case for employee engagement in their organisation.

What you'll hear: Real client stories, People Science in plain English, and practical next steps you can take back to your team.

title: (Season 4) P.Hood Talks -The Talk of The Hood- : Blood, Bricks, and Brotherhood
author: Tony Fair
description:
Welcome to Season 4 of P.Hood Talks: Blood, Bricks, and Brotherhood. After spending Season 3 unpacking the trauma and mental barriers in Hood Psychology, Mr. P.Hood is pivoting from the mind to the concrete. A healed mind sitting in a broken environment without an execution plan won’t change your reality. In this highly anticipated premiere episode, "The Foundation," we strip everything down to examine the actual structures we are building in our lives and our communities.

This episode breaks down the three core pillars of the new season. First, we confront the "Blood" we inherit and shed—challenging the community to stop bleeding for zip codes we don't own and start pouring that energy into a lasting family legacy. Next, we look at the "Bricks," shifting the focus from simply hustling to strategically laying a foundation for real wealth, real estate, and enterprise. Finally, we dissect "Brotherhood," separating genuine, accountable loyalty from the illusion of trauma-bonded street associations.

It is time to evolve the hustle and rewrite the code. Whether you are navigating toxic family dynamics, re-evaluating your inner circle, or trying to turn street-level survival skills into boardroom execution, this episode lays the exact blueprint you need.

Lock in, turn the volume up, and start stacking with purpose. Make sure to subscribe and leave a review on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube, Acast, or wherever you get your audio. Share this premiere with a brother who needs to hear it, keep your mind sharp, keep your circle tight, and keep laying those bricks.

"Blood Savage: True Crimes of the Cross," a gripping exploration into the stories of intrigue, mystery, and justice found within the pages of the Bible. Join us on a riveting journey delving into the darkest and most enigmatic crimes recorded in biblical history.
In this immersive podcast series, we uncover the hidden truths behind infamous incidents like the murder of Abel by his brother Cain, the harrowing conspiracy of Jezebel against Naboth for his vineyard, the scandalous affair of King David and Bathsheba leading to murder, and many more gripping narratives from ancient times.
Each episode presents meticulously researched accounts, shedding light on biblical crimes often overlooked or veiled in moral lessons. We analyze the motives, unravel the mysteries, and explore the moral complexities behind these captivating stories.
Hosted by LaNyce, a biblical enthusiast, "Blood Savage" offers a unique perspective on these historical events. Through a lens that combines theological insights, historical context, and true crime analysis, we navigate the blurred lines between sin and justice, morality and transgression.
From treachery and betrayal to jealousy and revenge, each episode peels back layers of these ancient crimes, inviting listeners to ponder the timeless themes of human nature and the pursuit of justice in the face of darkness.
Whether you're a true crime aficionado, a history buff, or someone seeking deeper understanding, "Blood Savage: True Crimes of the Cross" promises a captivating and thought-provoking exploration into the criminal narratives hidden within the sacred texts.
Subscribe now to embark on an enthralling journey through the shadowy side of biblical history. Uncover the compelling stories of deceit, passion, and redemption that echo through the ages, only on "Blood Savage."

title: Getting In: Helping First Generation Low-Income Students Get Into College
author: Minds Matter National
description:
There’s no shortage of college admissions advice. Almost none of it was built for first-generation, low-income students.


Most of it assumes you have a parent who’s been through it, a counselor with time for you, and money for test prep and private coaching. If that’s not your reality, the rules can feel unwritten, and the advice can feel like it’s meant for someone else.


On Getting In, Minds Matter CEO Erika Halstead sits down with college admissions leaders, the people who actually decide who gets in, and asks the questions students like ours need answered. What matters right now? What’s changed since affirmative action ended? What should you focus on, and what can you stop worrying about?


Each episode explains how the system really works in plain language, with clear takeaways you can use. It’s for students, and for the mentors, families, and educators who support them.


Getting in isn’t the whole story, but it’s where it starts.

title: The listening commons
author: Dr aninda Sidhana
description:
Dr. Nimesh G. Desai on Mental Health, Psychiatry, Human Rights, and Society

How does Dr. Nimesh G. Desai understand the relationship Siddhanath reflects on listening, prevention, non-judgmentalitygical science, and society?

Dr. Nimesh G. Desai is an Indian psychiatrist and public mental health specialist with more than four decades of clinical, academic, institutional, and policy experience. Formerly Director of the Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Sciences in Delhi, he has worked at NIMHANS and AIIMS. His career has included contributions to mental health services, psychiatric education, substance-use policy, human rights, multidisciplinary care, and debates concerning biological, social, and cultural approaches to psychiatry.

In this interview, Scott Douglas Jacobsen, Dr. Nimesh G. Desai, and Dr. Aninda Sidhana discuss mental health as a medical, social, cultural, and humanistic concern. They examine psychiatric diagnosis, biological research, biomarkers, psychopharmacology, multidisciplinary care, human rights, cultural differences, and the risks of over-psychiatrization. Desai emphasizes care, humility in science, diagnostic restraint, and integrating biological and psychosocial perspectives, while Siddhanath reflects on listening, prevention, non-judgmentality, and humane treatment.

description:
Beyond the Lab is a podcast from SIUE’s Graduate School and Office of Research that takes listeners inside the scholarly work happening across campus — not just what researchers study, but the human story behind why they study it.


Each episode, Dean Chris Slaten and Dr. Liz Cali sit down with one faculty member or research team for a 30 to 45 minute conversation that covers three things: the work itself, explained accessibly for any curious listener; the personal journey that led the researcher there; and the broader question of what the research means for the world beyond the university.


Guests span every corner of SIUE — from a pianist documenting composers who have been left out of the classical canon, to a neuroscientist studying fruit flies to understand autism, to an engineer teaching machines to read medical scans. The unifying thread is a belief that research is not something that happens in isolation. It is driven by people, shaped by curiosity, and connected to questions that belong to all of us.

title: Dispatches: Animalia
author: Tamer Asfahani
description:
Checkpoint and EUGY have come together because we share the same belief: that children learn to care for the natural world by experiencing it, not by being told about it. 
EUGY make beautiful, biodegradable animal models that a child can build with their own hands. 
We make stories that let a child experience the world through the animal's senses. 
Together, the story and the model become something neither could be alone — a story you can hold.

Every EUGY animal inhabits a world they experience individually through their own senses. Our stories are written from the perspective of that world. There are no villains or heroes, no happy endings or sad ones. They are dispatches from the natural world. 

Each story is written from the animal's own senses. They are written to help us understand that what we see isn't necessarily what other species see. They help us frame a changing world through the eyes of those affected.

Our stories let a child experience the natural world through another animal's body before anyone tells them what to think. The animals don't explain themselves. They move through their environment and the child moves with them. The ecological meaning arrives through sensation, not instruction.

You can find a link to buy the featured animal on the story page directly from EUGY.

Farawati Human Mark - what it means: 
Each story has its own original music composition, like all the Checkpoint stories do. Nothing is made with or by AI.

If you like our stories:
Then feel free to explore over 18 hours of other Checkpoint stories based in your favourite videogames. 2x British Podcast Award finalists and with over 75 million plays worldwide, you'll be joining a expanding number of listeners that use our stories to unwind and grow.

title: Saragossa: A Story of Spanish Valor (Minna Caroline Smith Translation)
author: Benito Pérez Galdós
description:
Gabriel's desperate flight from the French army leads him to the beleaguered city of Zaragoza, where he confronts the horrors of the 1809 siege. In this gripping tale, Benito Pérez Galdós immerses listeners in the heart of a brutal conflict that tests the limits of human endurance and the spirit of resistance. As Gabriel witnesses the city's courageous defense against overwhelming odds, he becomes entwined in a web of bravery, sacrifice, and the fierce determination of its defenders. 'Saragossa: A Story of Spanish Valor' is more than just a historical narrative; it’s a vivid exploration of the struggle for identity and freedom during one of Spain’s darkest hours. Hosted by Gloriane and Bradley, this is a space to explore the connection between your body, mind, emotions, relationships, and the deeper parts of yourself that can get lost in the demands of everyday life.
Whether you're navigating a life transition, feeling disconnected or overwhelmed, questioning old patterns, or simply sensing that there's more to life than going through the motions, Glo & Behold invites you to discover what's possible when you begin to listen to yourself differently.
Through personal stories, thoughtful conversations, embodied practices, and practical insights, we explore:
* *Movement & Embodiment:* Reconnecting with your body, releasing stagnation, and discovering movement as a pathway to presence and possibility.
* *Consciousness & Self-Awareness:* Recognizing patterns, expanding perspective, and creating space for more intentional choices.
* *Nervous-System Awareness:* Understanding your responses to stress, building capacity, and finding your way back to balance without demanding perfection.
* *Desire & Conscious Relationships:* Exploring connection, boundaries, intimacy, communication, and the ways we relate to ourselves and others.
* *Personal Growth & Vitality:* Moving through uncertainty, discovering what genuinely supports you, and developing practices that make everyday life feel more fulfilling and alive.
This isn't about having all the answers, achieving permanent calm, or becoming someone else. It's about developing a deeper relationship with yourself, cultivating the capacity to meet life as it unfolds, and remembering that transformation doesn't always require a dramatic leap. Sometimes it begins with a single moment of awareness.
Each episode offers an invitation to reflect, experiment, and carry something meaningful into your everyday life.
*You don't have to have it all figured out to begin.*
Come as you are. Get curious. Find your foundation. Discover what becomes possible when you reconnect with yourself.

Democracy in Action: Justice, Advocacy & the Power of Community
A Podcast Presented by the Massachusetts Black Lawyers Association (MBLA)

Democracy is not a spectator sport, and justice is not simply an ideal—it is a responsibility we all share.
Welcome to Democracy in Action, a podcast presented by the Massachusetts Black Lawyers Association (MBLA), where we explore the intersection of law, democracy, civil rights, civic engagement, and community empowerment.
Designed for legal professionals, students, community advocates, emerging leaders, and everyday citizens, this podcast seeks to make complex legal and civic issues accessible, relevant, and actionable. Through engaging conversations with attorneys, judges, elected officials, civil rights leaders, scholars, and community changemakers, we examine the challenges facing our democracy and the collective work necessary to protect the Rule of Law and advance justice.

Each episode offers meaningful perspectives, practical information, and opportunities for action. We will explore voting rights and voter protection, constitutional freedoms, civic responsibility, judicial independence, racial equity, and the role each of us plays in strengthening democratic institutions. We will also highlight MBLA's programming, statewide coalition-building, Know Your Rights initiatives, youth engagement, and partnerships that turn advocacy into meaningful community impact.
Drawing on the MBLA's longstanding commitment to justice, professional excellence, and community service, and guided by the platform of Purpose, Persistence, and Power, this podcast is more than a conversation about democracy. It is an invitation to participate in protecting it.
Our goal is simple: to move listeners from awareness to understanding, from understanding to engagement, and from engagement to action.
Because democracy is strongest when everyone has a voice, justice is accessible to all, and communities have the knowledge and power to shape their future.

Since I was a young boy, I've always wondered the same question: are we truly free in our world today?

title: Curse of: America's Next Top Model
author: iHeartPodcasts and Glass Podcasts
description:
When America’s Next Top Model premiered in the early 2000s, it looked like a golden ticket: a glamorous TV show that could catapult aspiring models into fame. But two decades later, many contestants describe its aftermath as a curse. Hosted by pop-culture journalist Bridget Armstrong, Curse of America’s Next Top Model is a deep investigation into the hidden costs of reality television, and what the show’s legacy reveals about beauty, power, and the culture that cheered it on. 
Through conversations with dozens of former contestants, producers and crew members, Curse of America’s Next Top Model explores what happened behind the scenes on one of the most iconic and problematic reality shows of our generation.  
The series starts off by exploring how ANTM almost didn’t get made. You’ll get the real story behind the show’s most infamous controversies. Then, the models and producers pull back the curtain and talk about how the most outrageous photoshoots and runaways came together. You’ll hear from contestants who say ANTM saved their lives and from those who say it ruined theirs. The contestants also talk about how the body shaming they experienced on the show caused lifelong scars. Finally, we try to answer the question, is Tyra Banks the ultimate reality television villain?  
Curse of America’s Next Top Model takes you on an investigative journey to figure out if the so-called curse is real? And if so, what was the toll on the models, and us, the audience?

Each episode focuses on the honest, in-between moments: first festivals, early funding wins (and losses), imposter syndrome, creative pivots, and the practical decisions that can shape a career long before the spotlight arrives. description: Reliable diagnostics make a difference during the busiest parts of winter and summer, when appointment windows can fill quickly across Blairs and surrounding areas. For heat pump repair, technicians often examine the defrost cycle, check outdoor fan operation, test reversing valves, and confirm that auxiliary heat strips engage only when needed. Safety steps are just as important on gas equipment; during furnace repair, a typical visit may include checking ignition systems, cleaning flame sensors, confirming proper venting, and measuring carbon monoxide to verify safe operation. Many homes pair these calls with filter changes and quick thermostat reviews to keep comfort steady after the fix. If airflow is limited, air duct cleaning or sealing options may be discussed to help the system move air efficiently. Solutions Heating & Cooling provides scheduled visits and urgent help when equipment stops unexpectedly, with practical recommendations for equipment age, part availability, and next steps for homeowners in Danville, VA.

description:
An honest, unfiltered look at yoga and everything that comes with teaching it.
I’m Sarah White, and after years of teaching, training teachers and working in the yoga industry, I’ve got a few things to say. About what we’re taught, what happens when we actually start teaching, and what we end up questioning along the way. Including ourselves.
Expect conversations about movement, philosophy, money, the business of teaching and the bits we don’t always feel comfortable saying out loud.
Experience behind me, plenty still to learn, and no interest in pretending I’ve got it all figured out.

title: A Mind in Progress
author: Usher
description: A Mind in Progress is a podcast about understanding yourself, navigating everyday emotions, and finding healthier ways to deal with life's challenges. Through honest conversations about overthinking, stress, self-doubt, emotional well-being, and personal growth, each episode explores the thoughts and experiences that shape the way we live. This is a space for thoughtful reflection, practical ideas, and small changes that can make everyday life feel more manageable. You do not need to have everything figured out to move forward. Sometimes, understanding yourself a little better is already a meaningful step. Because a healthy mind is not about being happy all the time; it is about learning, adapting, and growing at your own pace.

title: Transmission of Truth
author: Outright Vermont
description:
Transmission of Truth is a youth-led podcast about the lived experiences of transgender Vermonters. 
Transgender people are the targets of a coordinated, intense hate campaign in the US. At the center are transgender youth. Vermont offers transgender individuals important protections, but prejudice and discrimination remain real barriers to living freely.
Through insight from experts and stories from the hearts of everyday Vermonters, we offer a window into the lived experiences of the trans community, and the broader issues that impact their daily lives.

title: Not My Narrative
author: Straw Hut Media
description:
Every society runs on stories it mistakes for facts. In America, those stories shape who gets help, who gets blamed, and who is left out. “Not My Narrative” is a podcast and essay series from Next City that debunks the pervasive myths that have been used to justify neglect, inequity, and the status quo — and elevates the people proving those myths wrong.

Each episode pairs a podcast with three original essays. Together, they trace the origins of one stubborn myth that’s been handed down through politics, schools, and culture; document the harm it causes; offer a counter-narrative rooted in truth and justice; and highlight the leaders who are driving positive change by living out a different set of assumptions.

title: Outside the Box
author: Jason Brenner
description:
Fast shipping and seamless supply chains don't just happen. They're built in moments of innovation, through tough calls, and by leaders willing to bet on what's next. Outside the Box from FedEx explores how the world's boldest logistics executives are making those leaps, in what may be the most transformative technological moment of our lifetimes. 
Each episode, host Jason Brenner, Senior Vice President of Digital at FedEx, sits down with the minds behind some of the world's most forward-thinking logistics operations, from retail giants, to the disruptors redefining what's possible with predictive analytics, warehouse automation, and digital strategy. 
If you're a supply chain leader, logistics professional, or anyone navigating the frontier of digital transformation, Outside the Box delivers the real talk, hard data, and human stories behind the technology changing our world. 
New video episodes available every two weeks on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube and wherever you watch or listen.

description:
Paradigm Sift is a podcast encouraging you to take a little pause from a the hectic life, ponder on where your life is heading. 
The talks are created to start a spark, may be to ignite a fire to in your heart and mind. These talks are attempts to give you a little wake-up call, to start your journey.
If we like it or not ,the life is passing by and every minute that has passed can not be lived again. And no matter how long the journey it starts with the first step. 
I hope Paradigm Sifts will encourage you to not take the first step, but to lead you to happy and fulfilled life.

Just stories, questions and different ways of looking at life.

title: Latte & Life
author: By Toast Social
description:
Sometimes the most powerful conversations don’t happen in planned interviews or big moments. They happen quietly, over coffee, over brunch, when people slow down and the conversation moves beyond the usual small talk. 
That’s the idea behind Latte & Life. 
It’s a podcast about real people and the stories that shaped them. The moments they’re proud of, the things they’ve overcome, and the experiences that changed the direction of their lives. The kind of conversations that happen naturally when someone feels comfortable enough to speak honestly.

title: Soul Path Insights
author: Amelie Chambord
description:
Life rarely unfolds as planned. Sometimes we’re growing. Sometimes we’re grieving. Sometimes we’re praying for direction while trying to get through Tuesday.


Welcome to Soul Path Insights, a podcast where faith meets everyday life. I’m Amélie Chambord, a writer sharing personal stories, biblical encouragement, and honest reflections on trusting God, navigating relationships, starting over, and finding purpose as we grow older.


These conversations begin with lived experience—including the uncomfortable moments I’m still learning from. Expect thoughtful questions, a little humor, and room to admit that loving God doesn’t mean we have everything figured out.


My hope is that you leave each episode feeling less alone, encouraged in your faith, and ready to take one meaningful step forward.


Come as you are. Let’s grow from here.

title: The Stronger Side
author: Alex john
description: The Stronger Side is a fitness podcast about building strength, staying active, and making healthier choices in everyday life. Each episode explores simple ways to improve your routine, develop better habits, and stay motivated without putting unnecessary pressure on yourself. From getting started with exercise to finding balance between fitness and daily responsibilities, this podcast keeps things practical, honest, and easy to understand. You do not need to be an athlete or have a perfect routine to make progress. Whether you are taking your first steps toward a healthier lifestyle or working to stay consistent, The Stronger Side is here to help you move forward one day at a time.

title: Karlosophies and the Creative Resistance
author: Karly Nimmo
description:
Karly Nimmo explores creative resistance from two very different angles: the internal, and the external.
The external form being: human creativity as a form of systemic and political resistance...  How can we reclaim creative agency is this age of AI? 
And the internal: Working through our own own personal creative resistance. How do we we move through our own self doubt, and the creative blocks that stop us from expressing ourselves.

title: Parsha-ly Crazy
author: Matthew Ponak, Joel Goldstein & Rebecca Croog
description:
Three friends. One Torah portion. A conversation that rarely goes according to plan.
Parsha-ly Crazy brings Rabbi Joel Goldstein, Dr. Rebecca Croog, and Rabbi Matthew Ponak together for lively conversations about the weekly Torah portion. Drawing on Jewish tradition, scholarship, mysticism, lived experience, and three very different perspectives, they follow the Torah wherever it takes them.
Expect ancient texts, big questions, disagreement, unexpected connections, terrible puns, occasional irreverence, and plenty of laughter. The conversation is intellectual without being stuffy, spiritual without taking itself too seriously, and accessible whether you’ve been studying Torah for decades or are just curious about what all the fuss is about.
*Rabbi Joel Goldstein* is a rabbi, teacher, and scholar with a particular love of Talmud, halakhah, and the classical Jewish tradition.
*Dr. Rebecca Croog* brings a thoughtful, dynamic perspective grounded in Jewish communal life, social responsibility, and the questions that arise when ancient texts meet the real world.
*Rabbi Matthew Ponak* is a teacher of Jewish mysticism, spiritual counselor, and author of Embodied Kabbalah , with a particular interest in Kabbalah, Hasidism, and the historical development of Jewish tradition.
